title: Around town: rickshaws, cabs & buses
goal: Haggle with a rickshaw driver, book and direct a ride-app driver, tell drivers where to turn and stop, ask how long a trip takes, and use buses and intercity coaches.
intro:
Getting around Sindh's cities means rickshaws and chingchis you haggle with, ride apps like Careem, inDrive and Yango, Karachi's red buses and Green Line, and the coaches that run up and down the Super Highway between Karachi, Hyderabad and Sukkur.

This unit gives you the words drivers and passengers really use, and two pieces of grammar that make you sound natural: **compound verbs** (**روڪي ڇڏيو** 'stop!', **ڇڏي ڏيو** 'drop me off', **لهي ويو** 'got off') and **لڳڻ** for how long or how much something takes: **ڪيترو وقت لڳندو؟** 'how long will it take?'.

grammar.title: Compound verbs: روڪي ڇڏيو، ڇڏي ڏيو، لهي ويو
grammar.body:
Sindhi often says an action with **two verbs**: the first in the 'having done' form (stem + ي, Unit 22) carries the meaning, the second — the **helper** — adds a shade and takes all the endings:

**+ وڃڻ** — change, completion, 'off/away' (mostly with intransitive verbs): **ٿي وڃڻ** 'become', **پهچي وڃڻ** 'get there', **لهي وڃڻ** 'get off', **سمهي وڃڻ** 'fall asleep'. In the past: پهچي **ويو**، لهي **وئي**.
**+ ڇڏڻ** — do it completely, get it done, or do it and leave: هتي **روڪي ڇڏيو** 'stop right here', وقت تي **پهچائي ڇڏيو** 'get us there on time', ڊرائيور اسان کي **ڇڏي ويو** 'the driver dropped us and left'.
**+ ڏيڻ** — for someone else: مون کي هتي **ڇڏي ڏيو** 'drop me here', **ٻڌائي ڏيو** 'just tell me'.
**+ وٺڻ** — for yourself: لوڪيشن **ڏسي وٺو** 'have a look at the location'.
**+ پوڻ** — sudden: ٻار **سمهي پيو** 'the child dropped off to sleep', **ڪري پيو** 'fell down'.
**+ رهڻ** — settle into a state: اندر **ويهي رهو** 'sit down inside'.

Compounds sound more natural than the plain verb in commands and in the past — **روڪي ڇڏيو** is what you'll actually say to a driver.

**Trap:** in the past, a compound with **وڃڻ / پوڻ / رهڻ** agrees with the **subject** (هوءَ لهي وئي), even if the first verb is transitive; with **ڇڏڻ / ڏيڻ / وٺڻ** the ergative rule applies (مون ٽڪيٽون وٺي ڇڏيون).

grammar.title: It takes (time, money): لڳڻ
grammar.body:
'It takes half an hour', 'it'll cost 500' — Sindhi uses **لڳڻ** ('to be applied, be spent'). The **time or the money is the subject**, and the verb agrees with it:

**ڪيترو وقت لڳندو؟** 'how long will it take?' — وقت is m sg → **لڳندو**
اڌ ڪلاڪ **لڳندو** 'it'll take half an hour' (m sg)
ويهه منٽ **لڳندا** 'it'll take twenty minutes' (m pl)
پنج سؤ رپيا **لڳندا** 'it'll cost five hundred'

The trip goes before it with **۾** or with the oblique infinitive + ۾: ڪوچ **۾** ٽي ڪلاڪ لڳن ٿا 'it takes three hours by coach'; اسٽيشن **پهچڻ ۾** هڪ ڪلاڪ لڳو 'it took an hour to get to the station'.

**Tenses:** future لڳندو / لڳندا · usually لڳن ٿا / لڳندا آهن · past **لڳو / لڳا**.

**Distance:** ڪيترو پري آهي؟ 'how far is it?' · ڏهن منٽن جو پنڌ 'ten minutes on foot' · **فاصلو** 'distance'.

**Trap:** don't make the person the subject — not مان اڌ ڪلاڪ لڳندس. It's **مون کي** اڌ ڪلاڪ لڳندو 'it'll take me half an hour'.

culture:
Rickshaws and chingchis have no meters: you **agree the fare before you get in**, and a bit of good-humoured bargaining is expected (**اهو ته گهڻو آهي!** … **چڱو، ساڍا ٽي سؤ**). Address the driver as **ادا** or **چاچا**, or **استاد** — the respectful word for any skilled driver or mechanic. Use **توهان** with older drivers; with young ones **تون** is fine once you're chatting.

Ride apps (Careem, inDrive, Yango, and Bykea for motorbike rides) are popular in Karachi and Hyderabad because the price is fixed — on inDrive you even name your own fare. Drivers often call to ask **ڪٿي آهيو؟** and want the nearest landmark rather than an address: **مسجد جي ڀرسان**، **پيٽرول پمپ وٽ**.

In Karachi, the **Green Line** BRT and the red **Peoples Bus Service** buses are cheap and air-conditioned; there are pink buses for women only, and on ordinary buses women sit at the front. Between cities, **coaches** and vans leave from the **ڪوچ اڏو** when full, and the Super Highway (M-9) gets you from Karachi to Hyderabad in about two to three hours — with a chai stop on the way.

tip.title: Will you go? هلندين؟ / هلندؤ؟
tip.body:
- Ask a young driver **… هلندين؟** (informal); an older one **… هلندؤ؟** (polite).
- Ask the price first: **ڪيترا وٺندين / وٺندؤ؟**
- Offer: ٽي سؤ **ڏيندس** (m) / **ڏينديس** (f) — and agree before you get in.

tip.title: Compound verbs: روڪي ڇڏيو، ڇڏي ڏيو
tip.body:
- Two verbs: stem + **ي** + a helper that takes the endings.
- **ڇڏڻ** = do it fully: روڪي **ڇڏيو** 'stop!' · **ڏيڻ** = for someone: ڇڏي **ڏيو** 'drop me' · **وڃڻ** = change, away: لهي **ويو** 'got off' · **پوڻ** = suddenly: سمهي **پيو**.

tip.body:

- Keep going: سڌو **هلندا رهو**.

tip.title: English verb + ڪرڻ in the past
tip.body:
- بڪ ڪرڻ، ڪينسل ڪرڻ work like ڪرڻ: in the past the **thing** decides the ending.
- گاڏي (f) بڪ **ڪئي** · رڪشا (m) بڪ **ڪيو** · ٽڪيٽون (f pl) بڪ **ڪيون**.
- The doer takes the ergative form: **مون**، **تو**، **هن**.

tip.title: It takes: لڳندو / لڳندا / لڳو
tip.body:
- The time or money is the subject: اڌ ڪلاڪ **لڳندو** · ويهه منٽ **لڳندا** · پنج سؤ **لڳندا**.
- Past: هڪ ڪلاڪ **لڳو** · ٻه ڪلاڪ **لڳا**. Usually: **لڳن ٿا**.
- The trip takes **۾**: پهچڻ **۾** · ڪوچ **۾**.
